This integration shows a **Saunum Leil sauna** in Gladys, through the Modbus
TCP of its control panel on your local network. **Never tested with a real
device.** Not affiliated with Saunum.

> **Safety.** A sauna gets very hot. Never start heating from afar without
> making sure nobody is inside and nothing lies on the stove. Turning on from
> Gladys is **off by default** and refused while the door is open; turning off
> does not depend on that option (the cases where it can still fail are listed
> below).

## What you get

A sauna in the Discovery tab, with:

- **Session on** (yes/no, read only) and the **state** as text ("Standby",
  "Scheduled", "Heating", "Ready", "Cooling down", "Waiting for the door", with
  ", alarm" when one is on);
- measured **temperature**, **humidity** (newer panel firmware only),
  **door** (opening sensor), **heater elements on**, **alarm** (yes/no);
- the **setpoint** (thermostat) and the **session time left** (minutes, newer
  firmware only);
- the **light** (on/off);
- two buttons: **Turn on (heat)** and **Turn off**.

No switch for the session: an "everything on" from Google Home, Alexa, HomeKit,
MCP or a scene does not reach the start button.

## Setup

1. At the control panel, turn on Modbus TCP and note its IP address (best
   kept fixed in your router).
2. In Gladys, open the Saunum integration, enter the **address** (for example
   `192.168.1.80`, or `192.168.1.80:502`) and, if you changed it, the
   **Modbus unit id** (1 by default).
3. Save, then add the sauna from the **Discovery** tab.
4. To start heating from Gladys, turn on **Allow heating from Gladys**, and
   check the **setpoint of the "Turn on" button** (80 °C by default), the
   **highest setpoint** (90 °C by default, 100 °C at most, the limit of the
   panel) and the **session duration of the "Turn on" button** (60 min by
   default, 60 to 720).

The panel may accept **only one Modbus connection at a time** (not confirmed
on a real panel): avoid using another Modbus client (Home Assistant, a script)
on it at the same time. The integration opens one connection at a time (a new
address waits until the previous connection, even one still being opened, is
closed), waits 1 s between two reads and 0.5 s before a command (the
recommended and the minimum spacing of the pysaunum library), and closes its
connection after 10 s without a request (pysaunum says the panel closes it at
20 s).

The panel is read every 30 s (10 s to 10 min), not more often after a restart,
a reconnection to Gladys, the "Test the connection" button or a Discovery
scan. Exceptions: a few seconds after each command, and every 10 s while a
turn off or a start from Gladys is being checked (see below).

There is one panel per integration: the device keeps its id when you change
the address (a new DHCP lease, a replaced panel). The Modbus registers hold no
serial number, so the integration cannot tell two panels apart: change the
address only for the same sauna.

## The commands

### Turn off

Writes "session off" (register 0 = 0) to the panel. It does not depend on the
"Allow heating" option, a heating command in progress, failed reads, or the
first read after a restart. It is always written (never "already off"), goes
before every read or command waiting in the queue, cuts a read already on the
wire, and a heating write not sent yet gives way to it. It only waits for a
write already on the wire or a connection being opened, and the 0.5 s spacing
after it.

It is accepted on the echo of the panel, then **verified by the reads**: the
panel is read 5 s and 20 s later, and every 10 s for up to 2 minutes, until a
read shows the sauna off. A read showing it heating again (with no start from
Gladys after the turn off) writes "off" again, 3 times at most, with a warning
in the logs and in the status ("a turn off did not take effect"). This may also
turn off a session started at the panel within those two minutes: that is
intended. When a start may still land after the turn off (sent without answer),
that guard lasts 2 minutes whatever the reads show, and is kept across a
restart.

Turn off is refused, or fails, when:

- the value is not 1, or the device is not the panel of this integration;
- the configuration is not loaded within 3.5 s of the click ("The configuration
  is not loaded yet"), or there is no valid address or Modbus unit id;
- the panel cannot be reached ("Not sent", check the sauna);
- the panel refuses the write (a Modbus exception; a busy panel, exception 5
  or 6, gets one more try);
- it is still waiting at 4.3 s (a write on the wire, a slow connection): "Not
  sent yet", it leaves as soon as possible;
- it left but the panel did not answer in time: "Sent, without confirmation".

### Turn on (heat)

Refused when:

- "Allow heating from Gladys" is off (checked on arrival and again right before
  each write);
- the configuration is not loaded, or has no valid address or unit id; the
  device is not the panel of this integration; the configuration changes during
  the command;
- another heating command is in progress, or a previous start is not confirmed
  yet;
- a turn off is in flight, waiting, or not verified yet by a read (or one is
  pressed during the command);
- the fresh read fails (unreachable, no answer, invalid data) or cannot be done
  within 3.5 s;
- the device does not carry the fingerprint of a Saunum panel (a register
  outside the range pysaunum documents), or a panel that served registers
  105-118 no longer does;
- an alarm is on, or an alarm register holds an unknown value;
- the door is open;
- the sauna is cooling down; on a newer firmware: the state is not "Standby"
  (or unknown), or the panel reports a reason not to start;
- the writes cannot all leave within 3.5 s of the click (estimated after the
  fresh read: then nothing is written). A slow panel (about 200 ms per answer
  or more) cannot take the setpoint, the duration and the start in that time:
  set at the panel the same setpoint and session duration as the
  configuration, so that only the start is left to write;
- the panel refuses a write (Modbus exception) or a write cannot be sent.

A session already on: nothing is written (accepted). Otherwise it writes the
setpoint of the "Turn on" button and the session duration of the configuration
(when the panel holds other values), then starts the session. If the start is
refused after the setpoint or duration was written, the message says so (the
session is not started).

**The start is then checked on the reads** (5 s, 20 s, then every 10 s until
checked, and every read while the session runs): the setpoint must not be 0
(the preset's) nor above the highest setpoint of the configuration as it is
now, and the duration must not be 0 nor longer than the one written (shorter
is accepted); on a newer firmware the active duration (register 106) must not
be longer either, and the time left must fit in it. Otherwise, when the reads
show the session never started, or when no read could check it within a
minute, a turn off is asked, with a warning in the logs and the status.

### Setpoint

A whole number from 40 °C to the highest setpoint. Refused when:

- the option is off, the configuration is not loaded or not valid, the device is
  not ours, or the configuration changes during the command;
- another heating command is in progress; a turn off is in flight, waiting or
  not verified yet; or a turn off was pressed less than 2 min ago;
- the fresh read fails or cannot be done within 3.5 s; the fingerprint is
  missing, or registers 105-118 are no longer served;
- an alarm is on or unknown; the current setpoint is unknown;
- the sauna cools down (register 109 when served; otherwise a session on with a
  setpoint of 0);
- the door is open: on a newer firmware in every state but "Standby"; on an
  older one, while a session is on;
- the write cannot leave within 3.5 s, or the panel refuses it.

The same setpoint already set: nothing is written. With no session on, "Turn
on" writes its own setpoint anyway.

### Light

On/off (0 or 1), after a fresh read with the fingerprint of a Saunum panel.
Refused when the value is not 0 or 1, the configuration is not loaded or not
valid, the fresh read fails or lacks the fingerprint, or the write cannot be
sent or is refused.

Every command answers within 4.3 s; a write the panel received without
answering in time is "Sent, without confirmation".

## Limits

- Never tested with a real panel: made-up register values only. The register
  map is the one of the pysaunum library (Home Assistant).
- Older firmware without registers 105 to 118: no humidity, no time left, no
  controller state (asked again every 30 minutes).
- Fan, sauna type, AutoLeil and the panel's other settings are not handled.

## Troubleshooting

- "The panel does not answer": check the address, that Modbus TCP is on, and
  that no other Modbus client holds the connection.
- "invalid data": the device at this address does not answer like a Saunum
  panel (a session or door register outside 0/1).
- A warning in the status ("the session started from Gladys did not keep its
  values", "a turn off did not take effect"): check the sauna; it stays until
  the next start from Gladys or a new configuration.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Saunum in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Saunum sauna | `section` | Nein | Shows a Saunum Leil sauna in Gladys through the Modbus TCP of its control panel on your local network: session, state, temperature, humidity, door, heater elements, alarm, setpoint, time left, light. Turning off does not depend on the option below; heating from Gladys (turning on and the setpoint) is off until you allow it, and is refused while the door is open or an alarm is on (the guide lists every refusal). A start from Gladys is checked on the next reads and turned off if the panel does not keep its setpoint and duration. Enter the address of the panel, save, then add the sauna from the Discovery tab. A sauna heats to a high temperature: never heat it from afar without making sure nobody is inside and nothing lies on the stove. Never tested with a real device. Not affiliated with Saunum. |
| Address of the control panel | `string` | Ja | Its IPv4 address (best kept fixed in your router) or host name, optionally followed by ":port" (502 by default). Modbus TCP must be on at the panel. The panel may accept only one Modbus connection at a time: avoid using another Modbus client (Home Assistant…) at the same time. |
| Modbus unit id | `number` | Nein | 1 unless you changed it at the panel. |
| Allow heating from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default. On: the "Turn on (heat)" button and the setpoint may start or change heating, after a fresh read of the panel (refused while the door is open, an alarm is on, or the panel reports a reason not to start; the guide lists every refusal). Off: they refuse every request. Turning off does not depend on this option. |
| Setpoint of the "Turn on" button (°C) | `number` | Nein | Written before each start from Gladys, never above the highest setpoint below. |
| Highest setpoint (°C) | `number` | Nein | Gladys never asks for more (90 °C by default; 100 °C, the limit of the panel, at most). |
| Session duration of the "Turn on" button (min) | `number` | Nein | Written before each start from Gladys: the panel stops heating after it (60 min by default, 60 to 720). If a read shows a duration of 0 or longer than this one while the session runs, Gladys turns the sauna off. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often the panel is read, in seconds (not more often after a restart; read again a few seconds after each command, and every 10 s while a turn off or a start is being checked). |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the feature names of the devices added from now on, for the state texts and for the command errors. |

## So installierst du Saunum in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Saunum erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-saunum:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-saunum](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-saunum).

Saunum benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Saunum ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
